nba_directive.reason_text: This client is on an FHA loan paying $234/mo in mortgage insurance that builds zero equity — that's the concrete financial pain to anchor on. The play is to quantify the PMI waste tied to their life goal, honor the delay, but pin a specific callback so the conversation doesn't go cold.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by naming the $234/mo PMI as wasted money — not a rate pitch, a structural problem
  - 'You're currently paying $234 every month in FHA mortgage insurance that doesn't reduce your balance by a single dollar — it just disappears'
  - Annualize it: $234 × 12 = $2,808/year going nowhere
  - Ask them to confirm their life goal (retirement timeline, debt freedom, a specific event) so you can attach a real dollar figure to the delay

- Quantify the cost of waiting in their specific terms
  - Calculate how many months until their callback date and multiply by $234 to show the PMI dollars burned during the pause
  - Example framing: 'If we revisit in 3 months, that's another $702 in insurance you'll never get back — I want you to know that number going in'
  - Do NOT invent a new rate or payment — tell them you'll run the exact conventional refi scenario when you reconnect, using live rates at that time

- Reframe the move: FHA → Conventional eliminates PMI structurally
  - This isn't about chasing a lower rate — it's about escaping a product that permanently charges mortgage insurance regardless of equity
  - Conventional loans drop PMI once LTV reaches 80%; FHA MIP often runs for the life of the loan
  - Their current P&I is $3,394 + $234 MIP = $3,628 effective monthly cost — the refi math starts there

- Honor the delay but pin a hard callback
  - 'I completely respect the timing — let's put a specific date on the calendar right now so this doesn't slip'
  - Propose a 10-minute call: offer two specific time slots, get a confirmed date in writing via text reply
  - Set a calendar reminder on your end and send a one-line confirmation text immediately after they agree

- Leave them with one number to sit with
  - 'Between now and our call, $234/mo is the floor of what this costs you to wait — the rate conversation is secondary to just stopping that bleed'
  - Keep the door open: 'If anything changes before then, text me and we move faster'
